clue.text: How unlike one's nearest and dearest!

definitions.text: How unlike one's nearest and dearest!

blocks.clueFragment: How unlike one's nearest and dearest!
blocks.note: surface reading: a sigh about someone who behaves nothing like the rest of their family
setter's reading: take 'nearest' literally, so the opposite is far off in distance or manner

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how little a person resembles their own close family.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'nearest and dearest' means family, but the clue wants the opposite of near in its plain spatial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distant or aloof is the opposite of close, and close kin are called nearest.

clue.text: Light red wood used for flower container

blocks.note: rose is a pale red colour
in the game of bowls the ball is called a wood

explanation.surface: Pale reddish timber has been turned into a vase for flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' looks like timber, but bowls players call their balls woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose-bowl is a wide round vessel for holding cut blooms in water.

clue.text: It should remind people to put me first

indicators.note: the instruction to place one word before the others sets the running order of the parts
says which part leads the word, ahead of the rest of the sentence

blocks.note: taken as written
men are people
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note telling people to give priority to the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as an instruction: write 'people to', then put 'me' in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake exists to bring something back to mind, which is exactly what a reminder does.

clue.text: First-class spinner gets movement through air

blocks.note: a spinning top is a toy that spins
flight is travel through the air

explanation.surface: A top-class spin bowler makes the cricket ball drift in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, and flight is a spinner's art, but here the spinner is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight describes the highest level or division, so it means of the best quality.

clue.text: One can barely finish her performance

definitions.text: One can barely finish her performance

blocks.clueFragment: One can barely finish her performance
blocks.note: surface reading: a performer who only just manages to get through her act
setter's reading: 'barely' means naked, so she ends her act wearing nothing

explanation.surface: An exhausted performer struggles to get to the end of her show.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose act consists of removing clothes ends it nude, in an entertainer's routine.

clue.text: Relation, for a season, produces play

blocks.note: first meaning: a relation is a story, and this is one told for the coldest season
second meaning: a late romance by Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A family member comes to stay for a season and puts on a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a relative, but it means a narrative, something related.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote a drama with this title, so the phrase names a stage work by him.

clue.text: His spelling's sound in essays I see about

definitions.note: the clue points at a man; the answer is his name

indicators.note: asks for the letter names as they are spoken, not as written
turned about, so the spoken pieces are put in a different order

blocks.note: said aloud, the word is the letter S followed by two letter As
taken as written
the letter C is pronounced like this word

explanation.surface: Someone notices a writer's sound spelling while reading through essays.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell the name out loud: eye, ess, ay, ay, see. Those letter names are found in 'essays I see' once the I is moved round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The man referred to by the pronoun bears the biblical name of Abraham's son.

clue.text: One river to Scot is the same as another

blocks.note: the Po is a river in Italy
taken as written
Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: One river, as far as a Scotsman is concerned, is no different from any other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another river, following on from 'One river'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is a river in the eastern US that flows past Washington DC.

clue.text: Canned music for instance excelling all others?

blocks.note: first meaning: a disc carrying ... sound
second meaning: best ever

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether recorded music beats every other kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone disc holds prerecorded songs, and as an adjective the word means the highest ever achieved.

clue.text: No restriction in bays, perhaps - calm sea areas

blocks.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse, given here by example
latitude is freedom from restriction

explanation.surface: Coastal bays are left unregulated beside quiet stretches of ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bays' looks like inlets of the sea, which fits the surface, but they are horses. The latitudes come after the horse, as freedom given to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse latitudes are subtropical ocean belts known for light winds where sailing ships were becalmed.

clue.text: Signal requiring soldier to take up arms

blocks.note: surface reading: a call for a soldier to go to war
setter's reading: the signaller literally raises their arms, holding flags in set positions

explanation.surface: A bugle call or order tells a soldier to go into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: This visual system conveys letters by the angles of two hand-held flags, so it is a means of signalling.

clue.text: From part of Greece reached via 3

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to Attica, the region around Athens
second meaning: 3 is TOP-FLIGHT, and the top flight of stairs leads to the roof room

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads 3-down not as 'first-class' but as the last flight of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things of Athens and its region, and the noun is a room under the roof.

clue.text: Muck's up, we hear - hence some brass round North

indicators.note: something placed round another encloses it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: bugles are brass instruments, a few of the brass section
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A band bungles a piece, and the brass section gathers round the north end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' only asks you to take 'Muck's' as 'mucks'; there is no homophone in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch a task is to make a mess of it, the same as mucking it up.

clue.text: He succeeds with money received, right?

blocks.note: income is money coming in
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man asks whether he has done well now that he has been paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeds' suggests doing well, but it means taking over from a predecessor.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer who takes up a vacated post follows on after someone, so he is a successor.

clue.text: Out of order? Not the king's doing it was said

definitions.text: Not the king's doing it was said

blocks.note: first meaning: improper or incorrect

blocks.clueFragment: Not the king's doing it was said
blocks.note: second meaning: from the old maxim that the king can do no such thing

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a disorderly act was blamed on the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'The king can do no wrong' was a legal principle that the sovereign cannot be at fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is out of order is improper, and the old legal maxim says a sovereign never commits it.

clue.text: Needed to compose English with clarity

definitions.text: Needed to compose English with clarity

indicators.note: to compose is to put together, here making a new arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A statement of what it takes to write good clear English.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to read and write is a prerequisite for producing clear written prose.

clue.text: Accuracy exactly overhead

blocks.note: as in 'right here', meaning exactly here
split as 'over head': a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness, and in a down entry 'over' places the first part above it

explanation.surface: Something is precise and positioned directly above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead' reads as one word but splits into 'over' and 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being correct and exact is the quality of being right, as in the precision of an answer.

clue.text: Sailor puts part of one, pack under another

blocks.note: a deck is a pack of playing cards
a hand is part of a person

explanation.surface: A sailor stows his kitbag beneath someone else's.
explanation.walkthrough: The positional words are loose: in the grid the pack sits above the body part, the two simply joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A deck-hand is a crew member who does manual work on a ship's deck, a seaman.

clue.text: Richard Murphy said to be an autocrat

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the name is judged by its pronunciation

blocks.note: Dick is the pet form of Richard
a murphy is slang for a potato, and a tater is another

explanation.surface: A man called Richard Murphy is reputed to be a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy' looks like a surname, but it is old Irish-flavoured slang for a potato, which is also a tater.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a ruler holding absolute power without constitutional checks.

clue.text: Operating, like, policemen, with large numbers

blocks.note: first meaning: in effect, as a law still valid
a hint along the way: policemen are in the Force
second meaning: arriving in great strength

explanation.surface: Police officers are at work, turning out in big numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Force is a common British name for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule that is in effect is current and valid, and a crowd that turns up strongly comes in great strength.

clue.text: Musicologist rather like Shaw?

blocks.note: first meaning: Sir George ..., compiler of the famous Dictionary of Music
second meaning: a shaw is an old word for a thicket or small wood

explanation.surface: A music scholar is compared to George Bernard Shaw, himself a music critic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaw' looks like the playwright, but it is a dialect word for a copse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir George Grove founded the standard music dictionary, and a small group of trees resembles a copse.

clue.text: Put nothing on top.of vehicle in a bit of wind

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top means placed first, above what follows

blocks.note: O looks like zero
a car is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave the roof of a vehicle bare in a gust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like weather, but it means wind instruments, as in an orchestra's wind section.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped flute is a woodwind instrument, so it is one item of the wind section.

clue.text: Firmly established, and encouraged by support

blocks.note: first meaning: fixed in place, like a plant in soil
second meaning: cheered on, as fans root for a team

explanation.surface: Something becomes settled once backers give it encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant fixed by its roots is settled, and to root for someone is to cheer them as a fan.

clue.text: Unusual, like the rest of the Constables

definitions.text: like the rest of the Constables

blocks.note: first meaning: unconventional

blocks.clueFragment: like the rest of the Constables
blocks.note: second meaning: police officers not out patrolling are away from their rounds

explanation.surface: One member of a family named Constable is unlike the others.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C suggests the painter's family; it is police constables, whose patrol route is a beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eccentric departs from the regular rhythm, and constables not patrolling are off their rounds.

clue.text: Could be the lad put her in bad position?

indicators.note: says the woman is tucked inside the run of words that follows, not built from pieces

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second, and the start of the third
surface padding: it completes the picture of a girl put in an awkward spot

explanation.surface: A boy wonders whether he has put a girl in an awkward spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be the lad' sends you hunting for a boy's name; the girl is hiding across 'be the lad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so it can stand for the pronoun referring to a female.

clue.text: A bird or two

blocks.note: surface reading: someone unsure how many birds there are
setter's reading: the one bird's name is made of the names of two others

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a single species whose name joins two shorter bird names.
explanation.definitionFit: The titlark is an old name for the meadow pipit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Admirer's light burden

blocks.note: surface reading: an easy load carried by a fan
setter's reading: an admirer is said to carry a flame for the beloved, and that lamp is the load

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' reads as 'not heavy', but it is the definition, a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held lamp gives light, and a hopeless admirer is said to carry one for the loved person.

clue.text: Such luxury might bring silly lad to vice

indicators.note: something silly is muddled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A life of luxury could lead a foolish boy into sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is Italian for 'the sweet life', a life of pleasure and indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase names an idle life of pleasure and indulgence, which is luxurious living.

clue.text: Second employer possibly giving satisfaction

blocks.note: surface reading: a person's other boss turns out to be pleasing
setter's reading: a second is the assistant in a formal fight, and 'giving satisfaction' is answering a challenge to honour

explanation.surface: Someone's second job's boss turns out to be a good one.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant in a formal fight engages a second and gives the offended party the honour they demanded.

clue.text: It may be long in NY State or just an inch elsewhere

definitions.text: It may be long in NY State

blocks.clueFragment: It may be long in NY State
blocks.note: first meaning: Long ..., off New York
second meaning: in Scotland an inch is a small isle, as in Inchcolm

explanation.surface: Something is long in America but tiny elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' and 'inch' look like measures of length; both are parts of names for pieces of land in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Island is the famous New York landmass, and inch is the Scottish word for a small isle.
